IRS990.Desc: FISCAL SPONSORSHIP PROGRAM: ESTABLISHED IN 2017, THE FISCAL SPONSORSHIP PROGRAM SUPPORTS COMMUNITY-LED RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND TECHNOLOGY INITIATIVES THAT ADVANCE THE PUBLIC INTEREST. THE PROGRAM SERVES AS A HOME FOR OPEN SOURCE SOFTWARE PRACTITIONERS, RESEARCH TEAMS, TECHNICAL COMMUNITIES OF PRACTICE, AND ADVOCATES WORKING TOWARD COMMUNITY-CENTERED FUTURES IN RESEARCH AND TECHNOLOGY. AS OF JUNE 30, 2025, THE PROGRAM FISCALLY SPONSORED 14 PROJECTS.(CONTINUED ON SCHEDULE O) IN 2025, MANY SPONSORED PROJECTS PRIORITIZED LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY IN RESPONSE TO A CHALLENGING FEDERAL AND PRIVATE FUNDING ENVIRONMENT. THESE EFFORTS LED TO INCREASED REVENUE DIVERSIFICATION THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW FUNDING STREAMS. READ MORE ABOUT THIS PROGRAM: HTTPS://WWW.CODEFORSOCIETY.ORG/FSP

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 11B
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION'S TAX ACCOUNTANTS PREPARE FORM 990 FOR REVIEW BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT. THE FINAL FORM 990 IS DISTRIBUTED TO ALL BOARD MEMBERS FOR THEIR REVIEW AND COMMENT BEFORE FILING.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 12C
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: AT THE BOARD MEETING DURING WHICH A NEW OFFICER OR DIRECTOR IS ELECTED, HE/SHE IS ASKED TO SIGN THE CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY FORMS PREPARED BY OUR ATTORNEY. AT THE ANNUAL MEETING, ALL DIRECTORS UPDATE THEIR FORMS FOR THE FOLLOWING YEAR. IF A CONFLICT ARISES, THE BOARD WILL DETERMINE THE APPROPRIATE COURSE OF ACTION AS PROVIDED IN THE CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY. THIS WILL INCLUDE REQUIRING DIRECTORS WITH CONFLICTS TO ABSTAIN FROM VOTING ON TRANSACTIONS WITH WHICH THEY MAY HAVE A CONFLICT, AND BOARD DELIBERATIONS TO DECIDE WHETHER TO ENTER IN TO A TRANSACTION, AND IF SO, TO ENSURE THAT THE TERMS OF THE TRANSACTION ARE REASONABLE.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 15
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: PURSUANT TO ITS EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION POLICY, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS REVIEWS THE COMPENSATION ARRANGEMENTS OF THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER, THE CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER (OR ANY PERSON PERFORMING THE FUNCTIONS OF THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER OR CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER, REGARDLESS OF TITLE), AND ANY EMPLOYEE WHOSE TOTAL ANNUAL COMPENSATION EXCEEDS $150,000, TO DETERMINE THAT THE ARRANGEMENTS ARE REASONABLE. IN MAKING THAT DETERMINATION, THE BOARD MAY CONSIDER THE FOLLOWING FACTORS, AMONG OTHERS: COMPENSATION LEVELS PAID BY SIMILARLY SITUATED ORGANIZATIONS FOR FUNCTIONALLY COMPARABLE POSITIONS; THE AVAILABILITY OF SIMILAR SERVICES IN THE GEOGRAPHIC AREA; INDEPENDENT COMPENSATION SURVEYS COMPILED BY INDEPENDENT FIRMS; ACTUAL WRITTEN OFFERS FROM SIMILAR INSTITUTIONS COMPETING FOR THE PERSON'S SERVICES. THESE DETERMINATIONS ARE MADE AT THE TIME OF HIRE, WHEN COMPENSATION IS MODIFIED, OR AT TERMINATION, AND ARE DOCUMENTED CONTEMPORANEOUSLY.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION C, LINE 19
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION'S GOVERNING DOCUMENTS, CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY AND FINANCIAL STATEMENTS ARE AVAILABLE AT HTTPS://WWW.CODEFORSOCIETY,ORG/RESOURCES OR UPON REQUEST. IN ADDITION, THE ORGANIZATION'S FORM 990 IS ALSO AVAILABLE UPON REQUEST AND AT WEBSITES SUCH AS GUIDESTAR AS SOON AS REASONABLE PRACTICABLE AFTER FILING WITH THE IRS.
